newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SEOUL STOCKS CLOSE DOWN, PROFIT-TAKING BITES.
newsitem.headline: SEOUL STOCKS CLOSE DOWN, PROFIT-TAKING BITES.

text.p: Seoul stocks finished lower on Tuesday on profit-taking, ending three consecutive days of gains, brokers said.
They expected the market to further undergo consolidation on Wednesday, absorbing much of the selling pressure above 760 points.
The composite stock index closed down 2.15 points to 762.92 with 35.2 million shares changing hands.
Losers led gainers 401 to 374.
"The rally has lost its momentum now that it has confronted strong selling pressure," said Kim Dae-hee of LG Securities.
"The daily trading volume has to reach 40 to 50 million in order to successfully climb over the barrier," he said.
Brokers said insurance shares, which led the market on Monday, lost strength on profit-taking. The insurance sub-index fell 1.07 percent to 3,798.98 points.
The insurance sector was propped up by a local report of a rise in applications for travel insurance following the Korean Air crash in Guam last week.
LG Insurance fell 500 won to 56,000 and Hyundai Marine and Fire Insurance lost 400 to 39,500.
Blue chips closed mixed with Samsung Electronics and SK Telecom rising and Korea Electric Power falling prey to profit-takers.
Samsung gained 600 won to 72,500 and SK Telecom gained 5,000 to 495,000 but KEPCO lost 700 to 26,500. Pohang Iron and Steel ended flat at 61,400.
Blue chips have benefitted from rotational buying by institutional and foreign investors, brokers said.
"Institutional buying of selected blue chips is expected to continue on Wednesday," said a broker at Kyobo Securities.

Shares of Kia Group units also ended mixed after rising on a recycled rumour that the group's chairman would resign, which was one of the conditions creditors demanded in exchange for emergency loans.
News that the finance ministry was raising the individual credit guarantee ceiling for subcontractors of Kia Motors and Asia Motors had little impact on the market, brokers said.
"Kia shares would move on Wednesday in accordance with news released regarding the group," said Kim of LG.
Kia Motors fell 200 won to 13,500 and Asia Motors added 150 to 4,850.

Kia Precision closed at a limit low of 9,500, off 800, as a rumour that the nation's two carmakers Hyundai Motor and Daewoo Motor planned to buy stakes of the firm, which boosted the stock last week, failed to materialise.
Brokers said Ssangyong Motors climbed on a news report that its German partner Daimler-Benz Ag had agreed to raise its stake.
A Ssangyong Group spokesman denied the report, but said the German company was evaluating the automaker's assets.
Ssangyong rose 130 won to 5,100.
Brokers said the announcement of first-half earnings of LG Chemical and Chohung Bank hardly had any influence on the market.

LG Chemical's net profit rose to 12.97 billion won from 11.59 billion a year ago and Chohung Bank's earnings climbed to 70.48 billion won from 63.85 billion. LG gained 400 won to 15,200 while Chohung fell 110 to 5,150.
"The results were pretty much in line with the market expectations," said Kim Young-bum of Seoul Securities. "So it was no surprise." -- JEAN YOON (822) 727 5643
